<system-reminder>
## Swarm Mode

You are now in "agent swarm" mode. The user may send tasks that require a large number of parallel subagents.

## Workflow

You do not need to use TodoList to record this workflow.

1. First, you may need to do a small amount of exploratory work before deciding how to divide the task across subagents. You may not need subagents during this exploratory phase.

2. After exploring, if you are convinced no subagent is needed to complete the task, tell the user why and wait for further instructions; otherwise, continue with the appropriate delegation.

3. Once you have enough context, do not handle the main work yourself. Use AgentSwarm with a `prompt_template` containing the `{{item}}` placeholder and an `items` array for the requested or appropriate number of subagents, partitioning the problem so each item gives one subagent a distinct part of the work. Pass `subagent_type` when the whole swarm should use a non-default subagent profile.

## Coordination

- Give each subagent a distinct scope of work.
- Avoid duplicating work across subagents.
- Avoid assigning conflicting changes or responsibilities to different subagents.
- Remember that subagents have your full capabilities. Do not overload their prompts with excessive detail; only describe the necessary background and each subagent's specific task.
- Unless the user explicitly specifies a lower limit, do not try to conserve the number of agents. AgentSwarm supports up to 128 subagents and queues launches automatically, so decompose work as finely as possible while keeping subagent responsibilities non-conflicting; combine tasks only when they are genuinely inseparable. If the subagents only need to read, inspect, or report back without making changes, their scopes may overlap slightly.
</system-reminder>

=== js-yaml-3-14-2 ===
title: 'chore(deps-dev): bump js-yaml from 3.14.0 to 3.14.2'
category: other
requirement: '## Context

  The development toolchain depends on `js-yaml`, and the repository needs the newer 3.14.2 patch level to keep maintenance dependencies current without changing chart behavior.

  ## Desired outcome

  Update the pinned development dependency from `js-yaml` 3.14.0 to 3.14.2 while keeping all runtime chart features and public APIs unchanged.

  ## Acceptance signals

  Contributors install the refreshed dev dependency set successfully, and no user-facing ECharts behavior changes as part of the version bump.

  '
=== label-layout-margin ===
title: Fix/label layout margin
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  Chart authors are hitting inconsistent label spacing and overlap behavior across pie charts and shared label layout code, especially around margins, stroke-aware bounds, and post-layout updates.

  ## Desired outcome

  Label layout should apply the same geometry rules everywhere so `minMargin`, `textMargin`, hidden-overlap handling, and final label bounds behave consistently after layout adjustments.

  ## Acceptance signals

  Labels keep the intended spacing, pie labels and shared axis labels no longer drift because of inconsistent margin math, and overlap prevention reflects the final rendered label geometry.

  '
=== labelline-smooth-reset ===
title: 'fix(label): fix labelLine `smooth` can not be reset'
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  Pie labels can keep a stale curved guide line after `labelLine.smooth` is turned off or reset to zero, so option updates do not faithfully reflect the current configuration.

  ## Desired outcome

  Changing `labelLine.smooth` back to `false` or `0` should fully reset the guide line to a straight path instead of preserving the previous smoothing.

  ## Acceptance signals

  After updating `labelLine.smooth`, the rendered label line immediately matches the new setting and does not retain an old smooth curve.

  '
=== license-headers-precommit ===
title: 'chore: add license headers and a script of pre-commit'
category: feature
requirement: '## Context

  Contributors currently have no consistent safeguard for Apache license headers, so missing headers can slip into the repository and only get noticed late in review.

  ## Desired outcome

  Add repository tooling that checks for required license headers before commit, including a `checkheader` workflow that surfaces missing headers clearly while leaving runtime chart behavior unchanged.

  ## Acceptance signals

  Contributors get an actionable pre-commit failure when a required header is missing, and maintainers can enforce header compliance without changing user-facing chart features.

  '
=== logscale-negative-exponent-rounding ===
title: 'fix(logScale): Fix incorrect rounding usage, and support data with big negative exponent.'
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  Log-scale charts with values that use very large negative exponents can still hit incorrect rounding paths, leading to unstable tick generation and misleading axis output.

  ## Desired outcome

  Log-scale rounding should handle extremely small values consistently so charts with tiny magnitudes remain numerically correct and readable.

  ## Acceptance signals

  A log axis fed with very small values no longer mis-rounds its scale, and the resulting ticks and labels stay stable across the supported exponent range.

  '
=== matrix-label-api ===
title: Fix matrix label API
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  Matrix users are seeing inconsistent label behavior because matrix labels do not reliably inherit shared text defaults, and coordinate locator ranges can become invalid in edge cases.

  ## Desired outcome

  Matrix labels should inherit `option.textStyle` the same way other labels do, and matrix coordinate lookup should handle invalid locator ranges predictably, including the `coordClamp` path instead of producing unusable results.

  ## Acceptance signals

  Matrix labels pick up the expected default text styling, and matrix coordinate calculations no longer fail or return confusing ranges when some locator values are missing or out of bounds.

  '
=== matrix-label-formatter ===
title: 'fix(matrix): fix matrix label formatter does not work'
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  Matrix users can declare label formatters, but those formatters are not actually being applied, which makes matrix labels ignore both template strings and callback-based formatting logic.

  ## Desired outcome

  Matrix labels should honor `label.formatter` consistently, including string templates and function formatters, and formatter callbacks should receive the expected matrix label context such as `name`, `value`, and `coord`.

  ## Acceptance signals

  A matrix label configured with either formatter style renders the formatted text rather than the raw value, and callback formatters receive the documented data they need.

  '

=== pie-tangential-noflip ===
title: 'feat(pie): add `tangential-noflip` rotation mode to keep labels tangential without flipping'
category: feature
requirement: '## Context

  Pie labels can follow the tangent of the slice, but the current tangential mode may flip labels upside down, which is undesirable for designs that prioritize stable reading orientation.

  ## Desired outcome

  Add a `label.rotate` mode named `tangential-noflip` so tangential pie labels stay aligned to the slice without flipping to the opposite reading direction.

  ## Acceptance signals

  With `label.rotate: ''tangential-noflip''`, tangential labels remain readable and tangential while avoiding the automatic upside-down flip.

  '
=== radar-clockwise-option ===
title: 'feat(radar): add `clockwise` option'
category: feature
requirement: '## Context

  Radar charts currently assume a single indicator ordering direction, which makes it awkward to match designs or domain conventions that expect the indicators to progress clockwise.

  ## Desired outcome

  Radar coordinate systems should support a `clockwise` option so authors can choose the direction in which indicators are laid out.

  ## Acceptance signals

  Setting `radar.clockwise` changes the indicator ordering direction without breaking label placement or the rest of the radar rendering contract.

  '
=== release-6-0-0-rc1 ===
title: 'chore: release 6.0.0-rc.1'
category: other
requirement: '## Context

  The 6.0.0 release candidate needs distributable artifacts and versioned packaging that reflect the current source accurately, otherwise downstream adopters cannot validate the release in a realistic way.

  ## Desired outcome

  Prepare the 6.0.0-rc.1 release outputs and metadata so the published bundles match the release-candidate source without introducing any additional behavior changes beyond the intended release contents.

  ## Acceptance signals

  Consumers evaluating 6.0.0-rc.1 receive coherent release artifacts, version strings, and packaged outputs that line up with the release candidate they are testing.

  '
=== release-merge-master ===
title: 'chore: merge release to master after releasing 6.0.0'
category: other
requirement: '## Context

  After cutting 6.0.0, the main branch still needs the release-side packaging and maintenance updates so future development starts from the post-release baseline rather than a partially merged state.

  ## Desired outcome

  Bring the post-release changes back onto the main line, preserving the released packaging and maintenance updates while keeping existing chart behavior unchanged.

  ## Acceptance signals

  Maintainers see the main branch aligned with the released 6.0.0 baseline, with no extra product-facing changes beyond the release merge itself.

  '
=== typescript-esm-compatibility ===
title: 'fix(types): remove export assignment to support typescript esm compatibility'
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  TypeScript consumers using modern ESM resolution are running into friction with the published declaration entrypoints, especially in projects that mix `import` and `require` semantics.

  ## Desired outcome

  The published package should expose type entrypoints that work cleanly for modern TypeScript module resolution, including distinct ESM and CommonJS declaration paths where needed.

  ## Acceptance signals

  Projects using current TypeScript ESM rules can resolve the package’s declarations without manual hacks, and mixed consumers still receive the correct type surface for their module mode.

  '
=== typo-cleanup ===
title: 'chore: fix typos'
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  The project has accumulated a handful of spelling mistakes and mislabeled identifiers in internal code and example data, which makes maintenance harder and leaves contributors second-guessing whether a name is intentional.

  ## Desired outcome

1	title: Fix/label layout margin
2	category: bugfix
3	requirement: '## Context
4	
5	  Chart authors are hitting inconsistent label spacing and overlap behavior across pie charts and shared label layout code, especially around margins, stroke-aware bounds, and post-layout updates.
6	
7	  ## Desired outcome
8	
9	  Label layout should apply the same geometry rules everywhere so `minMargin`, `textMargin`, hidden-overlap handling, and final label bounds behave consistently after layout adjustments.
10	
11	  ## Acceptance signals
12	
13	  Labels keep the intended spacing, pie labels and shared axis labels no longer drift because of inconsistent margin math, and overlap prevention reflects the final rendered label geometry.
14	
15	  '

1	title: 'fix(label): fix labelLine `smooth` can not be reset'
2	category: bugfix
3	requirement: '## Context
4	
5	  Pie labels can keep a stale curved guide line after `labelLine.smooth` is turned off or reset to zero, so option updates do not faithfully reflect the current configuration.
6	
7	  ## Desired outcome
8	
9	  Changing `labelLine.smooth` back to `false` or `0` should fully reset the guide line to a straight path instead of preserving the previous smoothing.
10	
11	  ## Acceptance signals
12	
13	  After updating `labelLine.smooth`, the rendered label line immediately matches the new setting and does not retain an old smooth curve.
14	
15	  '

1	title: 'feat(pie): add `tangential-noflip` rotation mode to keep labels tangential without flipping'
2	category: feature
3	requirement: '## Context
4	
5	  Pie labels can follow the tangent of the slice, but the current tangential mode may flip labels upside down, which is undesirable for designs that prioritize stable reading orientation.
6	
7	  ## Desired outcome
8	
9	  Add a `label.rotate` mode named `tangential-noflip` so tangential pie labels stay aligned to the slice without flipping to the opposite reading direction.
10	
11	  ## Acceptance signals
12	
13	  With `label.rotate: ''tangential-noflip''`, tangential labels remain readable and tangential while avoiding the automatic upside-down flip.
14	
15	  '

1	title: 'feat(radar): add `clockwise` option'
2	category: feature
3	requirement: '## Context
4	
5	  Radar charts currently assume a single indicator ordering direction, which makes it awkward to match designs or domain conventions that expect the indicators to progress clockwise.
6	
7	  ## Desired outcome
8	
9	  Radar coordinate systems should support a `clockwise` option so authors can choose the direction in which indicators are laid out.
10	
11	  ## Acceptance signals
12	
13	  Setting `radar.clockwise` changes the indicator ordering direction without breaking label placement or the rest of the radar rendering contract.
14	
15	  '

===== js-yaml-3-14-2 =====
title: 'chore(deps-dev): bump js-yaml from 3.14.0 to 3.14.2'
category: other
requirement: '## Context

  The development toolchain depends on `js-yaml`, and the repository needs the newer 3.14.2 patch level to keep maintenance dependencies current without changing chart behavior.

  ## Desired outcome

  Update the pinned development dependency from `js-yaml` 3.14.0 to 3.14.2 while keeping all runtime chart features and public APIs unchanged.

  ## Acceptance signals

  Contributors install the refreshed dev dependency set successfully, and no user-facing ECharts behavior changes as part of the version bump.

  '
===== validator-13-15-23 =====
title: 'chore(deps-dev): bump validator from 13.15.20 to 13.15.23'
category: other
requirement: '## Context

  The development toolchain also relies on `validator`, and the repository needs the newer 13.15.23 patch level to stay current without introducing any chart-level behavior changes.

  ## Desired outcome

  Update the pinned development dependency from `validator` 13.15.20 to 13.15.23 while keeping runtime features, output, and public APIs unchanged.

  ## Acceptance signals

  The refreshed dependency installs cleanly for contributors, and users do not observe any product-facing behavior difference from this maintenance update.

  '
===== typescript-esm-compatibility =====
title: 'fix(types): remove export assignment to support typescript esm compatibility'
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  TypeScript consumers using modern ESM resolution are running into friction with the published declaration entrypoints, especially in projects that mix `import` and `require` semantics.

  ## Desired outcome

  The published package should expose type entrypoints that work cleanly for modern TypeScript module resolution, including distinct ESM and CommonJS declaration paths where needed.

  ## Acceptance signals

  Projects using current TypeScript ESM rules can resolve the package’s declarations without manual hacks, and mixed consumers still receive the correct type surface for their module mode.

  '
===== release-6-0-0-rc1 =====
title: 'chore: release 6.0.0-rc.1'
category: other
requirement: '## Context

  The 6.0.0 release candidate needs distributable artifacts and versioned packaging that reflect the current source accurately, otherwise downstream adopters cannot validate the release in a realistic way.

  ## Desired outcome

  Prepare the 6.0.0-rc.1 release outputs and metadata so the published bundles match the release-candidate source without introducing any additional behavior changes beyond the intended release contents.

  ## Acceptance signals

  Consumers evaluating 6.0.0-rc.1 receive coherent release artifacts, version strings, and packaged outputs that line up with the release candidate they are testing.

  '
===== release-merge-master =====
title: 'chore: merge release to master after releasing 6.0.0'
category: other
requirement: '## Context

  After cutting 6.0.0, the main branch still needs the release-side packaging and maintenance updates so future development starts from the post-release baseline rather than a partially merged state.

  ## Desired outcome

  Bring the post-release changes back onto the main line, preserving the released packaging and maintenance updates while keeping existing chart behavior unchanged.

  ## Acceptance signals

  Maintainers see the main branch aligned with the released 6.0.0 baseline, with no extra product-facing changes beyond the release merge itself.

  '
===== license-headers-precommit =====
title: 'chore: add license headers and a script of pre-commit'
category: feature
requirement: '## Context

  Contributors currently have no consistent safeguard for Apache license headers, so missing headers can slip into the repository and only get noticed late in review.

  ## Desired outcome

  Add repository tooling that checks for required license headers before commit, including a `checkheader` workflow that surfaces missing headers clearly while leaving runtime chart behavior unchanged.

  ## Acceptance signals

  Contributors get an actionable pre-commit failure when a required header is missing, and maintainers can enforce header compliance without changing user-facing chart features.

  '

Done. Report for the assigned slug:

## logscale-negative-exponent-rounding

**Root cause:** `LogScale.getTicks` computed tick values as `fixRound(mathPow(base, val))`, where `fixRound = numberUtil.round` with a hardcoded default precision of 10. For data with big negative exponents (e.g. 1e-59), every tick collapsed to `0`, producing broken/unstable log axes. This matches upstream apache/echarts PR #21120 ("fix(logScale): Fix incorrect rounding usage, and support data with big negative exponent."), whose final state removes that unconditional rounding.

**Files changed (commit `c6a28a3` `impl: logscale-negative-exponent-rounding`):**
- `src/scale/Log.ts` — in `getTicks`, replaced `let powVal = fixRound(mathPow(base, val));` with `let powVal = mathPow(base, val);` (rounding now only applied via `fixRoundingError` for the `#4158` fixMin/fixMin and axis-break cases, using the original value's precision). Matches the upstream end state. No changes to `src/util/number.ts` or `src/scale/Interval.ts` were needed — the relevant pieces there were already landed by the prior `impl: cartesian-small-number-rounding` commit, which I built on without reverting.
- `agent_tests/logscale-negative-exponent-rounding/logScaleNegativeExponent.test.ts` — new focused jest test: builds a log y-axis with data around 1e-59…1e-69 (patterned after the upstream `test/logScale.html` case) and asserts ticks are all `> 0`, strictly increasing, exact powers of the base, and that extent covers the data; plus a moderate-small-values stability case.
- `requirement_patches/logscale-negative-exponent-rounding.diff` — staged diff (101 lines, non-empty).

**Verification:**
- Targeted test run (`npx jest --config test/ut/jest.config.cjs --roots …/agent_tests/logscale-negative-exponent-rounding`): 2/2 passed.
- Existing scale suite (`test/ut/spec/scale/*.test.ts`, includes log-scale extreme/small-value cases): 4/4 passed.
- `npx tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit`: exit 0.
- `git status --short` shows no remaining changes for the committed files (other agents' staged/untracked files left untouched).

**Caveats:** The Log.ts edit and test file already existed as uncommitted/untracked work in the tree when I started (presumably from a prior interrupted run of this same assignment); I reviewed them against the upstream PR diff, verified correctness by running the tests, and committed them. Upstream also updated visual-test scaffolding (`test/logScale.html`, `test/runTest/...`), which I intentionally did not port — it's screenshot-runner infrastructure, not source behavior; the agent_tests jest test covers the regression instead.

Done. Report for the single assigned slug:

## radar-clockwise-option

**Findings:** The current default direction, determined from HEAD code, is counter-clockwise on screen: `Radar.resize` computed `angle = startAngle + idx * 2π/n` and `coordToPoint` maps it via `y = cy - r·sin(angle)`, so increasing indicator index moves counter-clockwise. The rendering contract (axis name/label placement in `src/component/radar/RadarView.ts`, split lines/areas, `dataToPoint`/`pointToData`) all derive from `indicatorAxis.angle`, so flipping the sign of the per-index step propagates consistently with no view changes needed.

**State encountered:** The working tree already contained a complete, uncommitted implementation of this exact feature in `src/coord/radar/Radar.ts` and `src/coord/radar/RadarModel.ts` (from a prior run of this assignment — no other agent's commit covered it, and the only other radar file, `agent_tests/radar-style-precedence/tmp-clockwise-check.test.ts`, is explicitly marked "not committed" by its owner, so I left it untouched). I reviewed that diff line-by-line against the requirement, verified it is correct and complete, added my own regression test, and committed it.

**Files changed (commit `e4f86eb` "impl: radar-clockwise-option"):**
- `src/coord/radar/Radar.ts` — removed stale `// TODO clockwise`; reads `radarModel.get('clockwise') || false` in `resize` and applies `sign = clockwise ? -1 : 1` to the per-indicator angle step. Default (`false`) keeps the legacy counter-clockwise layout.
- `src/coord/radar/RadarModel.ts` — added `clockwise?: boolean` to `RadarOption`, `clockwise: false` to `defaultOption`, and forwards the value into each inner indicator axis option in `optionUpdated`.
- `agent_tests/radar-clockwise-option/radar-clockwise-option.test.ts` — new focused test: default layout unchanged, explicit `clockwise: false` matches default, `clockwise: true` flips angles, and `dataToPoint` output is mirrored across the start axis with identical radii.
- `requirement_patches/radar-clockwise-option.diff` — non-empty staged diff, written before commit.

**Verification:**
- `npx jest --config agent_tests/jest.config.cjs agent_tests/radar-clockwise-option/` — 4/4 pass (initial run caught my own inverted angle expectations in the test; fixed and re-ran green).
- `npx tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit` — clean.
- `git status --short` on my files — clean after commit; other agents' staged/untracked files ignored.

**Caveats:** None functionally. Note the requirement's mandate ("default must preserve today's rendering") dictated `clockwise: false` as the default, which the implementation honors; labels/split areas are direction-agnostic because everything keys off `indicatorAxis.angle`.

payload.resultSummary:
Both requirements are implemented and committed. Final report:

## matrix-label-api — commit `36b5cac`
Matches upstream apache/echarts PR #21108 ("Fix matrix label API"). Note: the working tree already contained an uncommitted partial application of this PR (MatrixView ecModel wiring, MatrixBodyCorner coordClamp/invalid-range fixes, `clearTmpModel` in util/model.ts); I verified those hunks against the upstream diff, completed the missing pieces, and committed everything together.

Files changed:
- `src/component/matrix/MatrixView.ts` — threads `ecModel` through render and sets `_tmpCellLabelModel.ecModel = ecModel` so labels inherit `option.textStyle` via `setTextStyleCommon`'s globalTextStyle fallback; `clearTmpModel` calls to avoid leaking the ecModel reference.
- `src/coord/matrix/MatrixModel.ts` — adds `coordClamp?: boolean` to `MatrixBodyCornerCellOption` (with upstream docs); corrected `MatrixCoordRangeOption` doc comments.
- `src/coord/matrix/MatrixBodyCorner.ts` — body/corner cell parsing uses `MatrixClampOption[kind]` only when `coordClamp` is set (default `none`); `expandRangeByCellMerge` now expands only on *valid* single-cell ranges (`!invalid && !invalid`) and null-guards `cell.inSpanOf` (previously threw on NaN locators).
- `src/coord/matrix/matrixCoordHelper.ts` — locator lists with >2 parts now treated as `[first, last]` instead of invalid; dev warnings wrapped in `__DEV__`.
- `src/util/model.ts` — adds `clearTmpModel` helper.
- `agent_tests/matrix-label-api/matrixLabelApi.test.ts` — new jest test (3 cases): textStyle fontSize inheritance on all matrix labels; missing/out-of-range locators yield NaN per-dim without crashing; `coordClamp` covers the entire column only when enabled.

Verification: `npx tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit` exit 0; targeted jest run: 3/3 passed.

## matrix-label-formatter — commit `e848a87`
Matches upstream commit `09c721ff` ("fix(matrix): label formatter not work", PR #21410), minus its visual HTML test (replaced by a jest test per repo agent-test convention).

Files changed:
- `src/component/matrix/MatrixView.ts` — applies `label.formatter` in `createMatrixCell`: function formatters are called with `{componentType: 'matrix', componentIndex, name, value, xyLocator, $vars}` and string templates go through `formatTplSimple` with the same params.
- `src/coord/matrix/MatrixModel.ts` — adds `MatrixLabelOption` (typed `formatter`) and `MatrixLabelFormatterParams`; `MatrixCellStyleOption.label` now uses `MatrixLabelOption`.
- `agent_tests/matrix-label-formatter/matrixLabelFormatter.test.ts` — new jest test (3 cases): string-template formatter on x/y labels; function formatter on body cell including callback context (`name`, `value`, `xyLocator`); function formatter on nested dimension cells.

Verification: `npx tsc` exit 0; formatter jest 3/3 passed; matrix-label-api jest re-run after this change: still 3/3 passed.

Caveats:
- The requirement YAML mentioned formatter context "name, value, coord"; upstream names the locator field `xyLocator` (not `coord`) — I followed upstream, as instructed.
- Upstream's visual test files (`test/matrix*.html`) were intentionally not ported; coverage lives in the jest tests under `agent_tests/`.
- Both `requirement_patches/matrix-label-api.diff` and `requirement_patches/matrix-label-formatter.diff` were generated non-empty; `git status` shows no remaining changes in my files (other agents' files untouched).

## logscale-negative-exponent-rounding

**Root cause:** `LogScale.getTicks` computed tick values as `fixRound(mathPow(base, val))`, where `fixRound = numberUtil.round` with a hardcoded default precision of 10. For data with big negative exponents (e.g. 1e-59), every tick collapsed to `0`, producing broken/unstable log axes. This matches upstream apache/echarts PR #21120 ("fix(logScale): Fix incorrect rounding usage, and support data with big negative exponent."), whose final state removes that unconditional rounding.

**Files changed (commit `c6a28a3` `impl: logscale-negative-exponent-rounding`):**
- `src/scale/Log.ts` — in `getTicks`, replaced `let powVal = fixRound(mathPow(base, val));` with `let powVal = mathPow(base, val);` (rounding now only applied via `fixRoundingError` for the `#4158` fixMin/fixMin and axis-break cases, using the original value's precision).
